title: Random forest and Cox regression give a five-transcription-factor colon cancer model
summary: Combining a Cox proportional hazards model with random forest ranking, the authors selected five transcription factors (HOXC9, ZNF556, HEYL, HOXC4, HOXC6) from TCGA colon cancer data and built a prognostic model. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank analyses separated low- and high-risk groups in four public GEO datasets (GSE39582, GSE17536, GSE37892, GSE17537). The work is computational on public data without experimental confirmation; the abstract gives patient numbers of 925 and 1584 for the validation sets.
ai_technology: Random forest feature ranking combined with Cox proportional hazards regression

evidence.tested: Validation of the TCGA-derived model on four independent public GEO datasets.
evidence.unknown: Biological role of the five factors and clinical utility; the abstract gives two different validation patient counts (925 and 1584); full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranks transcription factors by predictive importance for survival.
